newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Water groups set to post higher profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Water groups set to post higher profits.

text.p: British water utilities Anglian Water and South West Water continue the trickle of interim results for the sector with both companies expected to report higher profits and dividends in the next two weeks.
Dividends from Anglian, which reports on November 5, should be "fairly chunky," one analyst said.
South West Water, which follows on November 14, has already said it will pay out 11.8 pence, up 20.8 percent, now that hostile bids from Severn Trent and Wessex Water have been blocked.

Anglian is expected to turn in pretax profits for the half year of between 123 to 140 million stg, up from 125.8 million stg previously and pay out a dividend of 10.0 to 11.3 pence, compared with 8.9 pence.

Initial indications suggested that South West Water would produced half year profits of 57 million stg to 62 million stg, up from 54.0 million stg. South West Water made its dividend commitment and promised a 15 stg per customer rebate for June 1997 after the UK government said it was blocking the bids as against the public interest on October 25.
"There is a lot of pressure on water companies to deliver on dividends, particularly ahead of a general election," one sector analyst said.

The next general election must be held by May 1997 and the opposition Labour party, well ahead of the Conservative government in opinion polls, is highly critical of privatised utilities and has committed itself to a one-off windfall tax.
And industry watchdog Ofwat warned earlier this week about excessive dividends and said it might require written explanations from companies.

Thames Water, which reported a 15 percent rise in underlying half year profits last week, hiked its dividend to 11.2 pence per share from 9.2 pence, pointing out that part of the increase was due to a 10 percent share buyback in the summer.
"Water companies might be wary of the political scenario but I don't think they will feel they have to be minimalist because of Ofwat," the sector analyst said.
Anglian, considered a solid, long-term player by the market, will be watched for cost-cutting measures or streamlining of its international business.
It might also announce extra discretionary expenditure to benefit customers with the possibility of a share buyback for shareholders, analysts added.
South West Water, meanwhile, will be expected to indicate whether it intends to maintain the strong level of interim dividend growth at the full year, analysts said.
It will also be watched for indications on its strategy, which responses to the proposed bids suggested would be a focus on its core business and improving efficiency, analysts said.
"The company will be wanting to paint a very good picture after the bids fell through," one analyst said.
